summary: A repeated run step reaches an engraving with domove_attempting already zero. C hack.c:domove() suppresses its engraving-wear call unless domove_core() recorded a successful WALK/RUSH attempt; JS unconditionally smudges after every moved step, inserting rnd(5) before the expected mcalcmove draw. A second omission in engrave.c:read_engr_at() leaves running active after reading the engraving, so the hero continues two extra tiles into a wall. Repair the movement-success bookkeeping and the engraving run-cancellation contract together; the mcalcmove annotation is downstream.

source.branch: hack.c:2695-2709 and 2964-2968: an automatic movement continuation comes from allmain.c:moveloop_core() with gd.domove_attempting == 0 because the first domove() cleared it. Although the hero changes position, gd.domove_succeeded receives no DOMOVE_WALK/DOMOVE_RUSH bit, so domove() must skip maybe_smudge_engr(). At the same destination, a nonempty sensed engraving and svc.context.run > 0 require engrave.c:read_engr_at() to call nomul(0) after both messages and engraving-memory writes.
callers: cmd.c:set_move_cmd():1387-1399 sets DOMOVE_RUSH for H; cmd.c:rhack():3792-3801 calls the first domove(), establishing multi and context.mv. JS cmd.js:set_move_cmd():2104-2115 and executeMovement():2683-2717 provide this path.
allmain.c:moveloop_core():513-534 repeats domove() directly while multi > 0 and context.mv, without another set_move_cmd(); JS allmain.js:1515-1533 preserves that caller distinction.

hack.c:domove_core():2964-2980 records success before spoteffects(TRUE); hack.c:spoteffects():3379-3381 calls pickup(1), pickup.c:702-708 calls read_engr_at() when no object is present. The pinned replay stack reaches JS hack.js:4183, hack.js:4963, pickup.js:1206, and engrave.js:497 in that order.
dependencies: engrave.c:read_engr_at():317-405, including sensed-message branches, bounded display text, remembered/pristine text handling, and final nomul(0) when run > 0. JS engrave.js:423-505 currently omits cancellation; reconcile the whole function while wiring the existing hack.js:nomul() implementation.

hack.c:nomul():4161-4173 and end_running():4130-4158 clear multi, run, mv, travel, travelmap, sleep/invulnerability and the canned command queue. JS hack.js:1037-1051 and 884-901 already own these updates; do not replace nomul(0) with isolated run-field assignments.

hack.c:maybe_smudge_engr():3019-3030 and engrave.c:can_reach_floor()/wipe_engr_at() consume return values/state at the post-move boundary. Preserve their random calls for successful explicit WALK/RUSH attempts while restoring the source mask that excludes continuations.

cmd.c:set_move_cmd()/rhack()/dotravel_target() and allmain.c:moveloop_core() own initial versus repeated movement intent. Preserve their caller distinction and clear gd.domove_attempting after every domove() return.

mkmaze.c:maybe_adjust_hero_bubble():1929-1941 shares hack.c:domove()'s success-mask branch with maybe_smudge_engr(). It returns immediately off the Water Plane; on that plane a nonzero direction plus hero_bubble permits rn2(2) and bubble-direction writes. The function already exists in js/mkmaze.js:654, so wire it at the source call when restoring the whole domove() wrapper.

pickup.c:check_here()/pickup(), invent.c:look_here(), and allmain.c:moveloop_preamble() also reach read_engr_at(); preserve sensing, message/input ordering, and run cancellation consistently across those callers.

evidence: Pinned source provenance: git show a0986b8404a83d232bee4bd2b5a9433337cf2739:<path>; the upstream gitlink is 16ff59115315917b93185d026aeefea06db9b0f4, inspected with git -C nethack-c/upstream show. Replay and recording agree through RNG index 3520. At index 3521, step 19, C expects rn2(12)=3 from mon.c:mcalcmove():1164, while JS emits rnd(5)=1. The previous step has matching twelve-call upkeep slices, so this is the first extra call, not a mismatch inferred from aggregate totals.

At step 18's engraving More boundary the pinned JS state is moves=4, hero=(8,5), multi=80, context.run=1, context.mv=1, domoveAttempting=0. The destination engraving has type ENGRAVE (2), text "Move diagonally with b u n y", and eread=false because the second pline is awaiting dismissal. The observed call stack is read_engr_at -> pickup -> spoteffects -> domove_core.

C cmd.c:1396-1398 sets the attempt bit only when a movement command is dispatched. hack.c:2706 clears it after that first domove(); allmain.c:525-526 calls domove() directly for subsequent run steps. hack.c:2966-2967 ORs the attempt mask into domove_succeeded, and hack.c:2702 tests that mask before maybe_smudge_engr(). JS hack.js:3805-3808 has no success record and hack.js:4190 calls maybe_smudge_engr() unconditionally, despite the observed zero attempt bit. This deterministically explains the first extra rnd(5) before normal upkeep.

C engrave.c:396-402 prints the reading, remembers text, marks eread/erevealed, then calls nomul(0) when context.run > 0. JS engrave.js:497-504 performs the output and memory writes but returns without cancellation. Thus the same recording's step 19 keeps the C cursor at [7,6,1] and only the reading message, while JS reaches cursor [5,6,1] with "It's a wall." appended and moves=7. JS continued two westward moves beyond the engraving.

Implementation scope: restore the whole domove() wrapper and domove_core() success-record writes as a divergence fix, maintaining gd.domove_attempting and gd.domove_succeeded as distinct source values and preserving the source position-change condition and early-return behavior. Include the source-complete read_engr_at() correction and nomul caller wiring needed to stop the same run. Do not alter mcalcmove or insert compensating RNG calls.

Validation targets for the implementing worker: independent recorded cases with an engraving reached by the first explicit move versus a later automatic run/count continuation; an empty/unseen engraving case that preserves running; and a sensed engraving case that stops it. Preserve explicit-move smudge draws, skipped continuation draws, output/input boundaries, and all nomul state updates. The later step-29 decor-description refusal in the unchanged replay is a separate source boundary and no additional gain is predicted from the count-54 upper bound.
